fe_parents_fighting.text: Through your bedroom wall you hear {{name}} and your other parent fighting again. Doors slam. Somebody says the word "lawyer."

choices.knock: Knock and ask them to stop

outcomes.silence: They go quiet, embarrassed. Dinner is awkward but peaceful.
outcomes.snap: You're told to mind your own business. You do, loudly, with a slammed door of your own.

fe_parents_separate.text: Your parents sit you down at the kitchen table. They've been "growing apart." {{name}} is moving out this weekend.

fe_parent_affair_found.text: You see messages on {{name}}'s phone that were definitely not meant for your mother. The sender has a heart next to their name.

outcomes.confess: {{name}} cracks and admits it. A very quiet week follows.
outcomes.deny: {{name}} calls you dramatic and takes the phone away. You know what you saw.

fe_parent_affair_mother.text: You spot {{name}} in a corner booth with a man who is not your father. Their hands are doing a lot of talking.

outcomes.flustered: {{name}} introduces him as a "colleague." Nobody orders dessert.
outcomes.honest: {{name}} walks you outside and tells you everything. You'd rather not know, and also you're glad.

fe_parent_job_loss.text: {{name}} got laid off. The house feels different: fewer snacks, more sighing, a suit hanging by the door like an accusation.

fe_parent_job_loss_mother.text: {{name}} lost her job and is pretending it's a vacation. The pretending is exhausting for everyone.

outcomes.repaid: She lands a better job within months and pays you back with a hug and a card.
outcomes.gone: The money vanishes into bills. She's grateful. You're lighter.

fe_parent_remarriage.text: {{name}} announces she's engaged. You've met him twice. He laughs at his own jokes first.

outcomes.wise: Turns out you were right. He had a gambling habit. She thanks you through gritted teeth.
outcomes.wrong: He's a decent guy and you look like a brat. The wedding happens without you in the front row.

fe_parent_remarriage_dad.text: {{name}} introduces a new wife and, as a bonus, two kids you've never met. "You'll be one big happy family," he says.

choices.ask_rules: Ask who gets the big room

fe_stepsibling_meet.text: Your new step-sibling and {{name}} are already best friends. You're the odd one out in your own kitchen.

fe_stepsibling_rivalry.text: Your step-sibling ate the last of your birthday cake and {{name}} thought it was funny.

outcomes.win: You win by volume. Everyone gets sent to their rooms, you in a slightly better mood.
outcomes.lose: You lose in a way that involves frosting in your hair.

fe_sib_wedding_gift.text: {{name}} is getting married. The registry has a $2,000 espresso machine on it. Everyone is watching to see what you give.

fe_sib_wedding_speech.text: {{name}} asks you to give a toast at the wedding. Two hundred guests, an open bar, and your only material is childhood blackmail.

outcomes.killer: The room roars. The bride cries. You're the favourite sibling for at least a year.
outcomes.flop: The joke about the ex lands on the actual ex. Silence. Someone coughs.

fe_sib_borrow_norepay.text: {{name}} needs $2,000 "just until next month." That was the first sentence. The third sentence is "you're the only one I can ask."

outcomes.repaid: Shockingly, every cent returns, with a coffee on top.
outcomes.never: Next month comes and goes. So does the next year. The topic is now radioactive.

fe_sib_borrow_again.text: It's been a year and {{name}} still hasn't mentioned the money. Now they're posting vacation photos.

outcomes.pays: They wince and send a partial payment that night.
outcomes.blowup: It becomes a fight about 1998, the bike, and who Mom loved more.

fe_sib_rivalry_adult.text: At the family dinner {{name}} casually mentions a raise. You mention nothing. The silence is a competition.

outcomes.ahead: You win the round. Mom looks proud. {{name}} looks at the gravy.
outcomes.caught: Your exaggeration is publicly corrected by someone who remembers everything.

fe_sib_success_envy.text: {{name}} bought a house. A real one, with a garden. The family group chat is mostly fireworks emojis.

fe_sib_arrested_bail.text: The phone rings at 3 a.m. {{name}} has been arrested. It's a misunderstanding, they say. Bail is $5,000.

outcomes.grateful: {{name}} walks out, hugs you, and actually shows up to court.
outcomes.skips: {{name}} skips the hearing. The bond is forfeited and your phone goes quiet.

fe_sib_dui_call.text: {{name}} totalled a car after "only two beers." Nobody is hurt but the car and the pride.

fe_cancer_scare_mom.text: {{name}} found a lump. She's calling it "probably nothing" in the voice she uses when it's something.

choices.go_with: Go with her to the biopsy

outcomes.benign: Benign. She cries in the parking lot and buys you lunch.
outcomes.serious: It's cancer, caught early. The treatment calendar becomes your calendar.

fe_cancer_scare_dad.text: {{name}} has "a spot on a scan." He wants no fuss and has asked everyone not to tell your aunt.

choices.push: Push him to see a specialist

outcomes.fine: A scar from an old injury. He grumbles at the bill and at your nagging, but he's fine.
outcomes.treat: It's real. You help pay for the first round of treatment and hold his hand in the waiting room.

fe_parent_move_in.text: {{name}} can't manage the stairs anymore. The spare room is empty and your conscience is not.

fe_parent_care_burden.text: Looking after {{name}} is a full-time job on top of your actual job. Your sleep has been replaced by a pill organiser.

choices.respite: Take a week of respite care

outcomes.hold: You hold it together, barely. He squeezes your hand and says nothing, which says it all.
outcomes.snap: You snap at him over soup. You apologise for an hour. He forgives you in four seconds.

fe_dementia_mom.text: {{name}} looks at you kindly and asks which of the neighbours you are. Then she asks you to say hi to your father, who is no longer with us.

outcomes.clear: For a second she sees you. Tears, then a joke. Then she's gone again.
outcomes.upset: She gets frightened and you hate yourself. Lesson learned.

fe_dementia_dad.text: {{name}} calls you by your grandfather's name and tells you to be home before dark. You're fifty and it's noon.

fe_nursing_home.text: The doctors say {{name}} needs round-the-clock care. A good nursing home costs a fortune. A bad one costs a different kind of fortune.

outcomes.ok: It turns out fine. Clean, staffed, and a surprisingly good bingo night.
outcomes.bad: The place is understaffed and dim. You know it the first visit. You stay up late with guilt.

fe_nursing_home_visit.text: {{name}} lives in a care home now. Visiting day is Sunday. The plastic flowers in the lobby have seen worse.

fe_funeral_planning_mom.text: {{name}} has died. Someone has to choose the casket, the flowers, the order of speeches, and who sits where.

fe_funeral_planning_dad.text: {{name}} died. The funeral home hands you a brochure with three tiers. The cheapest tier is called "Dignified." The priciest is "Legacy."

fe_eulogy.text: {{name}} and you are asked who will give the eulogy for your parent. The pause is long enough to park a hearse in.

outcomes.moving: You say the thing you needed to say. Even the cousins cry.
outcomes.stumble: You lose your place and your voice. {{name}} stands next to you and finishes it.

fe_will_reading.text: The lawyer reads {{name}}'s will to a room of siblings who suddenly remember every grievance since 1987.

outcomes.win: After a long fight with lawyers you get a bigger share. The holiday cards stop coming.
outcomes.lose: You lose, pay the legal fees, and also lose your sibling.

fe_will_squabble.text: {{name}} wants the grandfather clock. You want the grandfather clock. Neither of you wants to say it is about Dad.

outcomes.you_win: Heads. The clock is yours. It does not tick the way you remembered.
outcomes.they_win: Tails. You shake hands. You miss the clock a little.

fe_estranged_relative.text: Your father's long-lost brother turns up at the door with a casserole and no explanation. "We should talk," he says. "Family."

outcomes.good: He tells stories nobody has told you. You end up laughing at the table.
outcomes.bad: By the second hour he needs a loan. The casserole was a down payment.

fe_estranged_sib_back.text: {{name}}, who vanished for years, sends a message: "I'm sorry. Can we talk?" The cursor blinks.

fe_secret_adopted.text: A dusty folder tells you what nobody did: you were adopted. {{name}} has been waiting thirty years to say it.

outcomes.found: An emotional afternoon with a stranger whose nose is yours.
outcomes.nothing: Closed files, dead ends, and a form letter. You keep the folder.

fe_secret_other_father.text: Over wine {{name}} lets slip that your father might not be your biological father. She waits for you to say something.

outcomes.confirmed: The test says what she hinted. The man who raised you is still your dad. It's complicated.
outcomes.bio: Turns out it was a rumour. She shrugs. Everything is somehow warmer.

fe_family_reunion.text: The annual family reunion is in a park with a bouncy castle, forty relatives, and one extremely competitive potato salad.

fe_reunion_feud.text: Two aunts stop speaking at the reunion over a casserole recipe from 1991. You are caught in the crossfire.

outcomes.peace: A truce is declared over cake. You are given a medal made of foil.
outcomes.fail: Both aunts now think you took sides. You did not. You are now their common enemy.

fe_elder_stories.text: An elderly relative tells the story of the winter she crossed three borders with a goat and a sewing machine. Nobody knows which parts are true.

fe_elder_recipe.text: An elderly relative hands you a recipe written on a napkin and says it is the only inheritance she has to give.

outcomes.perfect: It tastes exactly like childhood. You eat three plates and call her.
outcomes.burnt: You burn it. She laughs for ten minutes and then teaches you properly.

fe_home_sold.text: The family home is being sold. You walk through each room with a roll of tape and a trash bag, finding your whole childhood in drawers.

fe_home_clearout.text: {{name}} and you divide the contents of the house. It turns out the ugly lamp is worth $400 and neither of you wants it for the right reasons.

fe_sib_divorce.text: {{name}} shows up on your doorstep with a duffel bag. The marriage is over. "Just a couple of nights," they say.

outcomes.brief: Two nights, three bottles of wine, and a lot of crying. They find a place and thank you.
outcomes.stays: Two nights turn into two months. You rediscover the word "boundaries."

fe_sib_divorce_side.text: Both {{name}} and their ex are asking you to take their side. They each text you at midnight.

fe_sib_child_guardian.text: {{name}} once asked you to be guardian of their child if anything ever happened. Then, one terrible winter, something happens.

fe_parent_70th.text: {{name}} turns seventy. There's a party in her garden, a banner that says SEVENTY AND FABULOUS, and a cake that is, mostly, whipped cream.

outcomes.touching: She cries into her napkin. You've never seen her this proud.
outcomes.awkward: Mid-speech you realise you've been talking about yourself for three minutes.

fe_parent_70th_dad.text: {{name}} turns seventy and claims he doesn't want a fuss. There's a fuss. He pretends to be annoyed and secretly takes a second slice.

fe_mothers_day_guilt.text: It's Mother's Day. {{name}} has not mentioned it three times, which is how you know it matters.

outcomes.forgiven: You call at 9 p.m. She says "oh, it's fine" in the voice that is not fine.
outcomes.sulk: She sulks for a week and mentions it at every future holiday.

fe_fathers_day_guilt.text: It's Father's Day. {{name}} says he doesn't need anything, then drops hints about a particular grill.

outcomes.hurt: He is hurt but pretends to be cheerful. That is worse.

fe_holiday_fight.text: The holiday dinner begins with grace and ends with {{name}} shouting about who forgot to bring the ice. Someone's mother-in-law has opinions.

outcomes.calm: You steer the conversation to the dessert. It works. This time.
outcomes.backfire: Both sides turn on you. The peacemaker is always the target.

fe_holiday_politics.text: At the table {{name}} says something about politics that makes three people put down their forks.

fe_friend_family_crisis.text: {{name}}'s family fell apart this month. They show up at your door with two bags and a look that says they can't ask.

fe_friend_parent_funeral.text: {{name}}'s mother died. They asked, quietly, if you'd come to the funeral. You haven't owned a black suit since the last one.

fe_ex_in_laws.text: You run into {{name}}'s mother in the supermarket. She hugs you for a long time and asks, "How's your... heart?"

outcomes.good: She says they are well and happy. It hurts less than you expected.
outcomes.bad: She says they are doing wonderfully with someone new. You buy a lot of ice cream.

fe_ex_parent_died.text: You hear that {{name}}'s father died. He once taught you how to fold a fitted sheet. It meant more than either of you admitted.

outcomes.warm: Nobody makes a scene. You stand at the back, then you're hugged. It heals something.
outcomes.awkward: The new partner is there. Everyone smiles too hard. You leave before the cake.

fe_parent_driving_keys.text: {{name}} just took out a mailbox. He is eighty-one. He says the mailbox moved.

outcomes.accepts: He argues, then hands them over with great dignity. You drive him to the market every Friday.
outcomes.furious: He barely speaks to you for a month. He also walks to the bakery, which is good for him.
